title: Dear Refuge of My Weary Soul
description: Dear Refuge of My Weary Soul in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER OLD, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Anne Steele wrote these words. They were printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 502.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to WINCHESTER OLD; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Dear Re-fuge of my wea-ry soul, On Thee, when sor-rows rise, On Thee, when waves of trou-ble roll, My faint-ing hope re-lies.

lines: Dear Refuge of my weary soul,
On Thee, when waves of trouble roll,
To Thee I tell each rising grief,
Thy Word can bring a sweet relief
Hast Thou not bid me seek Thy face?
And shall I seek in vain?
And can the ear of pardoning grace
No, still the ear of saving grace
O may I ever find access

licence: Public domain: Anne Steele died in 1778.
credits: Words by Anne Steele (1717–1778), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to WINCHESTER OLD by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
